dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concise reasons for positions (e.g., A: 'it's my break and I work from home'; D: 'I get home late').
Negotiation is concrete and transactional (amount S$10, PayNow number, payment reference).
No needless repetition; turns mostly advance coordination.
A offers alternatives rather than conceding the new scheduling demand, keeping options explicit.
evaluation.final_reason: The household settled the issues about dishwashing and shared supplies and A's mitigation of smells: Agent A committed to "keep the fan on, cover pans and close doors while I cook" and proposed S$10/month for supplies; Agent B accepted and agreed to "rinse and put away shared dishes the same night and chip in for supplies," then arranged the PayNow transfer to A ("My PayNow number is 91234567. Monthly transfers are fine."). Quote: Turn 3-4 and Turn 7-8. The stove-access request remains unresolved: Agent D asked for a weeknight rotation (Turn 11) and Agent A explicitly rejected a strict rotation while proposing alternatives (Turn 12). No one accepted A's alternatives, so the scheduling conflict remains open.
position_change_notes: Agent B moved from complaint to acceptance/coordination: initially complained about smells, then agreed to A's proposal and arranged payment (Turn 2 → Turns 3–4, 7–9).
Agent A offered concessions on smell mitigation and proposed to manage supplies for S$10/month (Turn 1 → Turn 3), and provided PayNow details (Turn 6–8).
Agent C participated as coordinator on payment reference but did not change a primary demand (Turn 5 and 10).
Agent D introduced a new, unresolved demand for a weeknight rotation and did not receive agreement (Turn 11 → Turn 12).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1 — Agent A: "I'll try to cut the smells (use the fan, close doors, cover pans) if everyone agrees to rinse and put away shared dishes the same night and chip in for supplies." / Turn 2 — Agent B: "Fair. I'll rinse and put away shared dishes the same night and chip in for supplies, if you keep the extractor fan on, cover pans and close doors while you cook."

Turn 3 — Agent A: "Okay — let's do S$10 each per month. Transfer to me and I'll buy supplies. I'll keep the fan on, cover pans and close doors while I cook." / Turn 4 — Agent B: "Okay, S$10/month works. I'll transfer now — do you want me to send S$10 each month or just pay for this month now? Which account/name should I send it to?"

Turn 5 — Agent C: "Agent A—what account/name should Agent B send the S$10 to? PayNow okay?" / Turn 6 — Agent A: "PayNow's fine. I haven't given my PayNow ID yet — I'll share it now. Do you want me to say my mobile number here?"

Turn 7 — Agent B: "Okay, post your PayNow mobile number here. I'll transfer now and set up monthly transfers." / Turn 8 — Agent A: "My PayNow number is 91234567. Monthly transfers are fine." (Mutual, concrete agreement on payments and A's commitments to mitigate smells and cover pans.)

Turn 9 — Agent B: "I'll transfer S$10 now to 91234567 and set up monthly transfers. What name/reference should I use for the transfer?" / Turn 10 — Agent C: "Agent B—use 'Kitchen supplies - Agent B' as the reference." (Operational coordination; no substantive dispute.)

Turn 11 — Agent D: "I get home late and never get to use the stove on weeknights. Can we set a simple weeknight rotation so everyone gets a fair chance?" / Turn 12 — Agent A: "Agent D, I cook most nights — it's my break and I work from home, so I can't do a strict rotation. We can do a simple booking system (say tell everyone by 6pm if you need the stove) or each pick one guaranteed weeknight; which do you prefer?" (New, unresolved scheduling conflict: D's rotation demand is rejected and alternatives proposed but not accepted.)

substantive_insights: A frames trade-offs: A accepts smell-mitigation duties in exchange for others doing same-night dishwashing and chipping in for supplies.
Resolved items are procedural/monetary (S$10/month, PayNow transfer) and a behavioural commitment (fan/cover/close doors), which are amenable to speech-only settlement.

The stove-access issue is a different kind of incompatibility: a recurring allocation of shared time requires either rota or booking rules; A's practical constraint (works from home) blocks strict rotation.
The group successfully converted a diffuse complaint (smell, unwashed pan) into a specific, enforceable arrangement, but scheduling requires additional negotiation.
